title: Cross Hedging, Minimum Variance Hedge Ratio, Stock Index Hedging, and Metallgesellschaft Disaster
prerequisites: Understanding of basic long and short futures hedging mechanics
Concepts of covariance, variance, and standard deviation
Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM) beta intuition
learningOutcomes: Calculate the minimum variance hedge ratio h* = rho * (sigma_S / sigma_F) and determine optimal contracts N*.
Execute an airline jet fuel cross-hedge using heating oil futures.
Calculate index futures contract quantities to immunize an equity portfolio against systematic market decline.
Adjust portfolio beta dynamically without liquidating underlying stock positions.
Analyze the Metallgesellschaft $1.3B disaster to identify contango roll risk and cash margin liquidity drains.

sections.title: Cross Hedging and Minimum Variance Ratio
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Formulate optimal hedge ratio h* when underlying assets differ from futures contracts.
keyPoints: Cross hedging introduces basis risk from imperfect asset correlation.
Minimum variance ratio h* = rho * (sigma_S / sigma_F) eliminates rho^2 of portfolio variance.
Hull Example 3.2: 2M gallons jet fuel requires 37 heating oil futures contracts.

sections.title: Stock Index Futures Hedging & Beta Tuning
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Immunize equity portfolios from market declines and tactically adjust beta.
keyPoints: Index futures shorting N* = beta * (V_A / V_F) neutralizes systematic market exposure.
Adjusting beta from beta to beta* uses N* = (beta - beta*) * (V_A / V_F).
Hedging preserves stock-picking alpha while neutralizing market beta.

sections.title: Stack and Roll Liquidity Traps & Metallgesellschaft
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Demonstrate maturity transformation dangers and liquidity mismatches.
keyPoints: Rolling short-dated futures forward creates substantial roll risk in contango markets.
Daily marking-to-market margin calls drain cash, while physical forward gains remain unrealized.
Metallgesellschaft suffered a $1.3B loss due to forced liquidation during oil contango.

misconceptions.misconception: A hedge ratio should always be 1.0 (one barrel of futures per barrel of physical asset).
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: If futures volatility exceeds spot volatility (sigma_F > sigma_S) or correlation is imperfect (rho < 1), a 1.0 ratio overhedges and inflates portfolio variance.

misconceptions.misconception: Hedging an equity portfolio with index futures removes individual stock selection benefits.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Index futures hedge only broad market systematic risk. The portfolio manager remains fully exposed to unsystematic alpha from individual stock selection.

activeRecallQuiz.scenario: An equity manager holds a $10,000,000 portfolio with beta = 1.2. The S&P 500 index futures contract trades at 2,000 with a $250 multiplier ($500,000 contract value). To reduce portfolio beta to 0.6, how many contracts should be traded?
activeRecallQuiz.question: Given a $10,000,000 equity portfolio with beta 1.2 and $500,000 index futures, what specific transaction reduces the total portfolio beta to 0.6?

coreTakeaways: Apply h* = rho * (sigma_S / sigma_F) when hedging with correlated proxy futures; never assume 1:1 hedging.
Contract sizing N* = h* * (Q_A / Q_F) eliminates rho^2 of asset variance.
Shorting index futures neutralizes systematic market exposure without selling underlying stocks.
Portfolio beta can be adjusted tactically using N* = (beta - beta*) * (V_A / V_F).
Stack-and-roll strategies require massive cash liquidity reserves to withstand daily contango margin drains.
